cases.canonicalQuestion: Does delaying an ARO cancel Hidden Deployment or Camouflaged State?
cases.draftAnswer: Delaying an ARO with a Trooper in Hidden Deployment cancels Hidden Deployment. By contrast, merely delaying an ARO with a Camouflaged Marker does not cancel Camouflaged State; that state is canceled only when one of its listed cancellation conditions occurs.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a Trooper use Cautious Movement inside an enemy's Zone of Control without Stealth?
cases.draftAnswer: The Trooper may declare Cautious Movement if it is otherwise eligible, but without Stealth it does not suppress AROs when the movement begins or ends inside the LoF or Zone of Control of an enemy Model or Marker. In that situation, enemies generate AROs as usual.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Do you have to declare whether a HoloMask Trooper is Hackable?
cases.draftAnswer: Normally, a HoloMask bearer's real Unit Profile and capabilities remain Private Information. However, if the HoloMask Trooper enters or is inside an enemy Hacking Area, its player must declare if the Trooper lacks Hacker or Hackable status.

cases.canonicalQuestion: In a Coordinated Order, can Targetless or Deployable weapons choose different points when another participant uses a weapon that requires a target?
cases.draftAnswer: No. If one of the Skills in the Coordinated Order demands a Trooper, Marker, or mission objective as a target, all participating Troopers must act against that same single target. The Targetless or Deployable allowance to choose different points does not override that requirement in a mixed Coordinated Order.

cases.canonicalQuestion: What is a Tacball and how does it work?
cases.draftAnswer: A Tacball is a stationary Deployable Weapon used by Team-Ops Units. It declares a BS Attack or CC Attack against any Order declared by an active enemy Model—but not a Marker—within its Line of Fire or in Silhouette contact. It has Total Reaction, a Combi Rifle, and a PARA CC Weapon (-3). It does not activate other Deployable Weapons or Equipment, is removed after suffering Wounds equal to its STR 1, and must be represented by a 55 mm Tacball Token or another S4 model or scenery piece.

cases.canonicalQuestion: How does Request a Tacball work?
cases.draftAnswer: Request a Tacball is an Optional Attack Short Skill available only to a Trooper with Infinity Team-Ops, and it can be used only in the second Game Round. It requires no Roll. The Trooper places a 55 mm Tacball Token in Silhouette contact with any part of its route, chooses one unique, non-transferable item from the Tacball Chart, and applies that item at the end of the Order. The Token is Deployable Equipment and remains where deployed until the game ends, it is destroyed, or it is removed. Each player may use this Skill only once per game.

cases.canonicalQuestion: Can a Controller and its Peripheral (Synchronized) both use the same Panoply in the same Order?
cases.approvedAnswer: Yes—provided both Models are in Silhouette contact with the Panoply and the Peripheral remains in Coherency with its Controller. The Controller and Peripheral declare Use Panoplies as the same Short Skill, and each Trooper makes its own WIP Roll. Each successful Trooper independently gains D-Charges or rolls on the Panoply Chart. The rules do not limit a Panoply to one user per Order.
